subject: Nimbus outage follow-up: technical readout, rectification plan, and verification request
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shenoy <priya.shenoy@nimbus.com>, Alex Morton <amorton@sierrasys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbus outage follow-up: technical readout, rectification plan, and verification request

Hi Priya / Alex —

Thanks again for your patience while we completed a technical review of the outage that affected your inference endpoint on 2026-10-08 (09:05–09:38 UTC). Below is a concise customer-facing summary of what happened, what we changed, and how we’ll verify recovery with you. I’ve attached a short timeline CSV and a one-page RCA PDF; the patch we applied to the KV-cache evictor is attached as a diff for your ops team to inspect.

Executive summary:
- Root cause: an unbounded KV-cache eviction loop triggered by a sequence-length regression when a small subset of requests included an unexpected control token. That loop amplified memory pressure and caused the inference worker pool to fall behind; autoscaler cooldowns delayed additional capacity.
- User impact: increased tail latency and token timeouts for 07:05–07:38 UTC (NATS/ingest timestamps differ by a few seconds) resulting in partial degradation for 2 of your ten endpoints, affecting ~4.2% of requests.
- Resolution applied: the KV-cache eviction routine was patched to enforce a per-request eviction budget, and autoscaler cooldown logic was adjusted to allow emergency warm-ups when cross-node cache pressure spikes. Patch and timeline attached.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-10-08 09:03 UTC: first elevated token latency observed by our monitoring.
- 09:05 UTC: error bursts from two inference workers; memory climbed above 85%.
- 09:08 UTC: autoscaler attempted to add nodes but was rate-limited by cooldown policy.
- 09:22 UTC: emergency manual scale and temporary routing fallback activated.
- 09:38 UTC: steady state restored; traffic normalized by 09:44 UTC after cache warm-up.

Actions we took (short term):
1) Deployed kv-cache-fix.patch (attached) to limit eviction cycle work per request — deployed 2026-10-09 02:30 UTC.
2) Adjusted autoscaler policy to support emergency warm-up for cross-node memory pressure spikes — deployed 2026-10-09 03:05 UTC.
3) Implemented per-endpoint alerting thresholds to route traffic off degraded workers faster — in prod 2026-10-09 04:00 UTC.

Planned medium-term actions (owner / ETA):
- (Marissa) Add guardrail tests to the regression test harness to catch control-token variations — ETA 2026-11-02.
- (Hannah) Formalize autoscaler emergency-mode runbook and stress test schedule — ETA 2026-11-15.
- (Olga) Audit recent model onboarding checks that allow atypical token sequences and start a workstream to tighten input validation — ETA 2026-10-29.

Verification and ask from Nimbus:
- Can your ops team run the attached patch through your preflight review and confirm that it’s compatible with your deployment? If you prefer, we can provide a short remote walkthrough (20–30 minutes).
- We’d appreciate one or two synthetic request logs from your side showing sequence lengths during peak hours so we can validate the new guardrails against your workload.

I’ve also opened OPS-4921 (link below) and shared the timeline/RCAs in Drive. If you’d like a live readout, we can schedule a 30-minute technical session next week.

Attachments: 20261009-nimbus-timeline.csv, 20261009-nimbus-rca-summary.pdf, kv-cache-fix.patch

Thanks — we take this seriously and want to make sure your traffic is stable.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Morton <amorton@sierrasys.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Priya Shenoy <priya.shenoy@nimbus.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 14:05:23 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus outage follow-up: technical readout, rectification plan, and verification request

Sergio — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick items from our side:

1) We’ll have our security/process team look at kv-cache-fix.patch this afternoon. Expect a short note by EOD PST.
2) For verification, do you need raw request payloads or anonymized sequence-length histograms? We prefer to avoid sharing PII.
3) Can you confirm whether the autoscaler change requires any config updates on our side, or is it fully handled by Redwood?

On the impact: it would be helpful if you could include a short note about estimated customer-facing retries and whether any token bills will be adjusted for the affected window.

Thanks — Alex
Ops Lead, Sierra Systems
amorton@sierrasys.com | +1 (415) 555-6220

Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:02:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus outage follow-up: technical readout, rectification plan, and verification request

Alex — thanks. Answers inline and next steps.

1) Security review: great — please share any comments on the patch. We purposely kept the change small: a per-request eviction budget and a circuit-breaker so long-running evictions stop and surface a diagnostic.

2) Verification artifacts: anonymized sequence-length histograms are sufficient. If you can provide peak-hour histograms for the last 7 days (UTC), that will let our regression harness exercise the same distribution. We do not need PII or full request bodies.

3) Autoscaler change: no config changes required on your side. The change is fully contained in the Redwood control plane and rollout was automatic for your account; we only toggled a cooldown override flag server-side. We will provide the runbook excerpt that documents this behavior.

Billing/credits: Marissa — can you confirm the retrospective credit proposal for the 09:05–09:44 UTC window (2 endpoints impacted, estimate 4.2% of requests)?

Next steps / proposed plan:
- Nimbus ops: share anonymized histograms (Priya) — ETA 2026-10-14.
- Redwood: provide runbook excerpt and the patch changelog — ETA 2026-10-12 (link posted to Drive).
- Joint testing call (optional): 30 minutes; available slots 2026-10-16 14:00 or 2026-10-17 09:00 PDT.

We’ll hold the patch under a feature-flag until we validate with your histograms; if you want we can schedule a canary with 5% traffic first.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Priya / Alex —

Quick note on credits and verification cadence. I propose the following:

Credit proposal: 5% usage credit for the affected 40-minute window, applied to your November invoice. This is conservative relative to our internal estimate and intended to avoid delaying your internal reconciliation. Sergio — if that’s acceptable, I’ll create a billing ADJ-3924 and loop in Finance for processing.

Verification cadence: once Priya sends the histograms and we complete the small canary run (5% traffic for 1 hour), we will request one verification sign-off email from Nimbus confirming no observed regressions during their peak window. If Nimbus prefers, we can convert that sign-off into a short post-canary checklist call (10 minutes).

Priya — let me know if you want me to start the billing ticket. Also, if you want our SRE to join the canary window for live monitoring we can arrange that.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
